title: deferred cancel, session rehydration, and server deadline propagation for streaming (OpenAI bridge)
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: production apps using long-lived streaming sessions saw two related classes of failures: 1) aggressive client-side cancel requests that raced with in-flight tool/function calls causing opaque partial outputs, and 2) reconnects that dropped important server-side deadlines leading to silent tokenization/decoding truncation. This PR introduces: (a) a deferred-cancel token that lets the server finish in-flight tool calls or gracefully truncate output within a short grace window rather than abruptly terminating the stream, (b) a session rehydration path on reconnect that replays minimal session state (last acked token, KV-cache prefetch hints, and outgoing toolcall markers) to restore streaming continuity, and (c) explicit propagation of server-side deadline/deadline-extension headers through the OpenAI compatibility bridge so downstream clients observe consistent timeout semantics. Changes are implemented to be opt-in behind the config flag "streaming.deferred_cancel_enabled" and the OpenAI-bridge header "X-OpenAI-Bridge-Deadline". Checklist: - [x] implement deferred cancel token and server-side grooming logic - [x] add reconnect rehydration RPC and minimal session snapshot - [x] propagate and normalize deadline headers in openai bridge - [x] add unit and integration tests (server + bridge + SDK smoke) - [x] docs and migration notes - [x] staged rollout plan and a kill switch for emergency revert Notes on behavior: deferred cancel does not block user-initiated immediate aborts for admin/hard-kill requests; it only delays soft/local cancels for up to N ms (default 500ms) to allow idempotent toolcalls to finish or to emit a structured truncated payload. Session rehydration is intentionally minimal: we only reapply last-acked token index, KV keys for a small prefix window, and toolcall IDs that are still pending as per the session tombstone. Rehydration uses a handshake to avoid replaying completed side-effects. OpenAI bridge: we map internal deadline metadata to X-OpenAI-Bridge-Deadline and include an "x-rw-session-state" opaque token to help SDKs detect resumption. Testing: new integration tests simulate network disconnects at various points in streaming (mid-toolcall, during function result emission, during structured JSON block). We also added a small load profile test showing median 95th latency increase of 2ms for typical short requests and average success rate improvement for reconnects from 82% -> 96% on our synthetic trace. Rollout: enable flag in canary region for 48h, monitor reorder/duplicate toolcall metrics and structured-output validation errors; after verification enable globally. Related work: ENG-9412 (streaming stability epic), ENG-9499 (openai bridge compatibility fixes). See design RFC: https://go.redwood.design/rfcs/streaming-deferred-cancel (internal). Merge notes: squash-merged after CI rerun and one follow-up fix for a flaky test in test_rehydrate.py; added release note for API behavioral change and config flag. Migration: SDKs should respect X-OpenAI-Bridge-Deadline and treat session-resume tokens as opaque; no forced SDK update required but recommended to pick up new SDK helper to surface resume diagnostics.

release_notes: Introduces a 'deferred cancel' soft-abort mode for streaming that reduces partial/opaque outputs on client cancels; session resume support for better reconnect behavior; and propagates server deadlines through the OpenAI-compat bridge.
